prompt:
Document type: adjuster_file. Page 1 of 2.

<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1056
Claimant:
Timothy Middleton
Adjuster:
Alison Sweeney
December 12, 2023
First notice of loss reecived for a low-speed head-on collision involving the insured vehicle. The claimant reports a
wrist injury and is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.
January 7, 2024
Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that coverage is in force on the reported loss date. No coverage
questions have been identified at this stage.
January 21, 2024
Police report obtained. Officers confirm the claimant was present in the vehicle at the scene, and the report's
description of the collision matches the initial statement.
March 3, 2024
Statements taken from two independent witnesses, both of whom describe the crash the same way the claimant and
the other driver did. Scene photos were also reviewed and are consistent with that account.
March 13, 2024
Inspected the insured vehicle. Damage to the front end and airbag deployment line up well with the reported impact,
and the repair estimate has been opened.
April 3, 2024
Reviewed the medical records. The wrist fracture is consistent with the type and force of this collision. Treatment has
run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, so the file will be monitored as records arrive.
April 22, 2024
Prior records show a minor strain in the same area many years ago, which resolved fully with no ongoing limitation.
Noted for the file and for the medical reviewer.
May 4, 2024
At a follow-up, the claimant added some small details to the account of the accident. The core sequence of events
has not changed from the original statement.
May 18, 2024
Photos of the vehicle show a few older scratches in areas not clearly tied to this impact. Their age is not yet
established, so the appraiser has been asked to note them separately.
July 7, 2024
A neighbor contacted the desk and believes the vehicle was already damaged several weeks before the reported
date. This is a single unverified remark and has been logged for follow-up wtihout being treated as a finding.
July 9, 2024
Next steps are to request the remaining treatment records through counsel, obtain the appraiser's supplement on the
older marks, and schedule a review of the neighbor's comment before any settlement discussion.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
JSON format:
